items.title: India's Smartphone Exports Just Hit a Record $9.84 Billion
items.summary:
India shipped out nearly $9.84 billion worth of smartphones between April and June this year, a 23.4% jump and a new quarterly record, with smartphones making up 64.8% of all electronic goods exports. Apple was the single biggest driver: India's iPhone exports hit a record ₹2 lakh crore in FY26, making Apple the country's single largest branded exporter across any product category.

items.title: India Puts Up ₹80,000 Crore to Finally Crack Deep Water Oil
items.summary:
India is putting up an ₹80,000 crore war chest under Samudra Manthan to change how it explores for offshore oil and gas, offering to fund up to half the cost of deep water wells that can run over ₹1,000 crore each. India imports roughly 85% of its crude oil, and deep water reserves are one of the few real levers to change that.

In this episode of Front Page, we break down the 18 deep and ultra-deep water blocks up for auction under Open Acreage Licensing (bidding extended to September 17), ONGC's first appraisal well already spudded in the Mahanadi basin, and why this marks a shift from penalising companies for not drilling enough to the government sharing the financial risk itself.

items.title: Rayalaseema Just Landed Kia, DRDO, and an Enormous Steel Giant
items.summary:
Rayalaseema sits in the Deccan Plateau's rain shadow, missing both monsoons, and has historically been one of India's driest, famine-hit regions. It's now being written up as one of the country's newest industrial hubs, with Kia's only Indian plant, Royal Enfield's first factory outside Tamil Nadu, DRDO's AMCA testing facility, Bharat Forge's defence unit, and JSW's ₹16,350 crore steel plant all landing in the same belt.

In this episode of Front Page, we break down the state's shift from "ease of doing business" to "speed of doing business," the push into horticulture and food processing as the next growth layer, and the debate over Andhra Pradesh's government amplifying a national newspaper's coverage of its own record in near real-time.

Gartner projects that fewer than 15 agents per enterprise in 2025 could become more than 1.5 lakh by 2028, creating a governance challenge around identity, access, cost, security and accountability. The conversation also examines who owns an agent’s decisions, how CIOs can build governance before 2028, and why enterprise AI value depends on domain context and measurable business outcomes. items.title: Anthropic's Unreleased AI Just Cracked a NIST Quantum Encryption Finalist
